classification.summary: RewardVaultDelegator.initialize() was left callable on the deployed delegator, letting the attacker overwrite admin and then point setImplementation() at its own contract to sweep user allowances.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

sources.note: onchain review: victim 0x7bACB1c805CbbF7c4f74556a4B34FDE7793d0887 created 2023-03-01T08:23:57Z by 0xe9547cf7e592f83c5141bb50648317e35d27d29b, which is not the attack-tx sender 0x8ebd046992afe07eacce6b9b3878fdb45830f42b; 0 EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the victim before the incident; code age measured from deployment (onchain).

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis, and the implementation swap seen at the incident block is the attack itself. RewardVaultDelegator keeps `implementation` at storage slot 0; it held the deployment value 0x3d11015d9044cabbb2504448e37f20d0d56e36f8 from creation through block 32820951 and only moved to 0x5366c6ba729d9cf8d472500afc1a2976ac2fe9ff inside the exploit block 32820952, where the sole NewImplementation event also fires (slot 1 `admin` is overwritten in the same block). callTracer shows the delegator executing 0x3d11015d... before and 0x5366c6ba... after the takeover, so the code the attacker hit is the deployment-time implementation.
